rationale: Repair of the observation channel and re-execution of the same sourced question. The first retained execution (99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e) completed with exit code 0 and produced six CA_EVENT lines, but the runner recorded every one of them as invalid_observation ('Event must be an object with an event name') because the harness emitted the event name under an 'alias' key; no comparison was evaluated and all seven comparisons returned unknown with no result event reached. The harness now emits the required 'event' name field (fixture, construct, live) and nothing else about the fixture, admissions, comparisons or assertions changed, so the successor experiment isolates the emission repair and requests a fresh execution of the identical scenario. The question-level account is restated to keep the first receipt as a retained channel failure that establishes no comparison result.

experiment.revision_reason: Observation-channel repair only: the first run's CA_EVENT objects carried the event name in an 'alias' field, so the runner rejected all six lines as invalid_observation and no comparison had a result event. The successor emits the same fields under the required 'event' key; fixture, modes, admissions, identity fields, assertions and controls are unchanged.
semantic_changes: CA_EVENT objects now carry a string 'event' field naming the event (fixture/construct/live) instead of an 'alias' field, so the runner can parse them into observations.
The emitted field sets, event order, modes, store fixtures and comparison definitions are otherwise identical to the previous experiment.

scope.description: Restart-shaped construction of a single node (LocalID A, ProtocolVersion 3, in-memory log/stable/snapshot stores) whose last snapshot predates a committed configuration entry, observed with RestoreCommittedLogs off, on (construction only), and on with background goroutines started.
assumptions: The stores, configuration contents and their indexes are supplied by the harness: snapshot index 5 with configuration {A,B,C} at configuration index 1, log entries 1..7 with a LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} at index 6, and a persisted commit index of 7 (StageCommitIndex), which is a state a follower can reach after committing a configuration change and crashing before taking a newer snapshot.
The FSM discards applied entries and its Restore accepts the snapshot bytes; snapshot restore therefore succeeds and lastApplied after restore is the snapshot index.
For the two construction cases conf.skipStartup is true, so no background goroutine runs and r.configurations is read directly as the state NewRaft computed.

For the live case the node runs normally (default timeouts, no reachable peers) and the sample is taken only after the node has entered the candidate loop; the public GetConfiguration copy is read instead of r.configurations.
excluded: The election/quorum consequence is not executed here: no election with a majority of the current configuration and a minority of a stale one is run.
The snapshot was produced by the harness rather than by a live Snapshot() call, so the fixture's log/snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced.

experiment.prefix: For each mode the harness creates a fresh InmemTransport("A"), InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots); it writes a version-1 snapshot at index 5, term 1 with configuration {A,B,C} at configuration index 1 and closes the sink; it stores log entries 1=LogConfiguration{A,B,C}, 2..5=LogNoop, 6=LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E}, 7=LogNoop; it calls logs.StageCommitIndex(7). It then emits a 'fixture' event describing those stored facts, builds Config with DefaultConfig(), LocalID "A", a null logger and RestoreCommittedLogs set from the mode, and calls NewRaft(conf, fsm, logs, stable, snaps, trans). In the two construction modes conf.skipStartup is left true, and a 'construct' event reports lastApplied, commit index, latest/committed configuration id sets and indexes, quorumSize, hasVote(self), the number of batches queued on fsmMutateCh and the number of FSM restores. In the live mode the background goroutines run; a 'live' event reports the public GetConfiguration id set, the node state and current term. Modes run in the order baseline, restore_committed, restore_committed_skip_startup_false so the emitted event order is fixture, construct, fixture, construct, fixture, live; every CA_EVENT object carries its event name in the 'event' field.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft startup path: NewRaft's configuration scan (api.go) combined with the RestoreCommittedLogs replay (api.go restoreFromCommittedLogs -> raft.go processLogs); the node is responsible for using the configuration of the latest configuration entry in its own log.

knowledge.assertion: scan start index is max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1
restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) before the scan, advancing lastApplied

comparisons.description: Feature on: the constructed node's latest configuration should be the membership of the committed configuration entry at index 6 in its own log.
Feature off control on the identical stores: the same assertion about latest configuration.
Feature on: the node's election quorum should be the majority of the five voters recorded by the committed configuration entry.
Feature off control: quorum from the same log.
Mechanism operand: with the feature on, the replay advanced lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the configuration scan.
Mechanism operand control: without the replay lastApplied is the snapshot index, so the scan covers index 6.
Running node with the feature on: the configuration reported through the public GetConfiguration should be the committed membership, sampled while the node is campaigning.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store's persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go 724-753) reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 = commit+1 (api.go 610-620), so a committed LogConfiguration entry stored in the node's own log is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. The node keeps the snapshot's membership in both r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed, and since a candidate's threshold and a node's voter set come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) while vote requests are admitted from the receiver's own configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), the restarted node's election quorum is sized from the older membership. The condition does not self-heal along the observed paths: duplicate entries are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1526-1553), so a leader that already has this follower's log matched does not cause the entry to be re-processed, and configurations are refreshed only by new entries or an installed snapshot (raft.go 1955-1962). The first retained receipt for this question (99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e) completed with exit code 0 but carried no usable observation: all six CA_EVENT lines were recorded as invalid_observation because the harness named the event under 'alias' instead of the required 'event' field, so none of the seven comparisons had a result event and all returned unknown. That receipt is retained as a channel failure and establishes no comparison outcome; the successor experiment filed in this update changes only the emitted event-name field and requests fresh execution, and the account therefore remains conditional on that receipt. Bounds that do not depend on the receipt: the fixture's log and snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced by a live node, the multi-node election with a minority of the true configuration was not executed, the node still stores the newer configuration entry in its log, and the second registered question (constructor replay backpressure) is independent of this account.
limitations: The minority-quorum election consequence is derived from source (quorumSize and vote admission) and has no executed multi-node witness yet.

The experiment supplies the durable state (snapshot index 5 with configuration {A,B,C}, log entry 6 = LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E}, StageCommitIndex(7)) rather than producing it with a live cluster, so fixture reachability rests on source reasoning.

Persistence of the stale configuration is argued from the duplicate-skip in AppendEntries and from the absence of another configuration refresh path; it was not observed on a long-running node with an active leader.
The first retained receipt (99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e) has zero parsed result events and cannot support any comparison outcome.
Only in-memory store types and the module's own constructors were used; no repository test and no on-disk log store were exercised.
counterevidence: The node does store the newer committed configuration entry in its log (the FSM batch for indexes 6 and 7 is queued), so the stale membership is an unprocessed entry rather than a missing one.

The feature's documented purpose (config.go 243-255) is to replay committed logs into the FSM, so changing the scan start index may have been intentional; the account rests on the resulting membership state, not on the intent.
